run.question:
Customers reported slow checkout for the last hour. Check our Datadog APM
traces for the checkout-service and find which downstream call is slow.

report.summary: The requested source, Datadog APM, is not available in this Run: Datadog is not among the available data sources (available: jaeger, prometheus, kubernetes, elasticsearch; not_integrated lists only change_history), so no Datadog APM trace data could be queried. The APM-equivalent backends on the registered target m0-otel-20260909 were also unreachable: every Jaeger trace query and every Prometheus query attempted (service list, span search, span search by tags, metric-name discovery, instant query, range query, target list, rule list) returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, and the Elasticsearch/OpenSearch endpoint held no indices, so span/client-call latencies such as rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_* or http_server_request_duration_seconds_count could not be read and no latency ranking of checkout's downstream calls exists in this evidence. What the reachable evidence does show: the checkout pod's own logs for the last hour contain only successful PlaceOrder → payment → confirmation sequences with no error/timeout line, and in the sampled 16:55:53Z–17:11:16Z sub-window the internal step deltas are 12.5–21.6 ms (PlaceOrder to 'payment went through') and 5.7–13.3 ms (payment to 'order confirmation email sent'); payment, shipping, quote and cart pods show millisecond-scale handling of the same requests; all otel-demo pods are Running with restartCount 0 and were started 14:36–14:38Z, i.e. before the incident hour, so no restart or rollout occurred in it. No downstream call is therefore identified as slow, no service is named as affected, and no root cause is assigned. Since these log deltas are application step timings for roughly 40 visible orders and not RPC-level latency for all traffic, they neither confirm nor rule out a slow downstream hop.

claims.text: checkout-6578865d87-v6flf in namespace otel-demo emitted 294 log lines of its own JSON application log between 2026-11-23T16:52:14Z and 17:52:14Z; the newest 200 lines cover 17:11:16.848Z–17:51:58.775Z and consist solely of repeated '[PlaceOrder] user_id=… user_currency=…' → 'payment went through (transaction_id: …)' → 'order confirmation email sent to …' sequences, with no error, failure, timeout or deadline line.

In the earlier sampled sub-window 2026-11-23T16:55:53Z–17:11:16Z (93 checkout log lines), the delta from each '[PlaceOrder]' line to the following 'payment went through' line was 12.5–21.6 ms and the delta from 'payment went through' to 'order confirmation email sent' was 5.7–13.3 ms for every one of the ~31 complete sequences shown.

The payment pod payment-6f7bc865d6-wwqnm logged 'Charge request received.' followed by 'Transaction complete.' 1.0–1.6 ms later for each sampled charge between 2026-11-23T17:41:01Z and 17:51:58Z, with matching transaction ids to the checkout log entries (for example transaction_id 9ddb48ba-00eb-466d-96e3-345034891bc8 at 17:51:58.763–.764Z).

The shipping pod shipping-6fc5f694db-968zl logged 'Received quote: …' followed by 'Sending Quote: …' within about 0.05 ms and 'Tracking ID Created: …' roughly 5–6 ms later for each sampled order in 2026-11-23T17:41:41Z–17:51:58Z.

The quote pod quote-75774ddb4c-qq27v logged 40 sampled 'POST /getquote HTTP/1.1" 200' responses at 2026-11-23T17:24:41Z–17:51:58Z with no non-200 status shown, i.e. shipping's own dependency answered successfully on those requests.

The cart pod cart-549b8757d-7492d logged ValkeyCartStore AddItemAsync/GetCartAsync/EmptyCartAsync entries spaced 1–13 ms apart across its newest 40 lines (2026-11-23T17:50:49Z–17:51:58Z), i.e. no multi-second stall inside cart's Valkey operations on those requests.

All 22 pods in namespace otel-demo (including checkout-6578865d87-v6flf, payment-6f7bc865d6-wwqnm, shipping-6fc5f694db-968zl, quote-75774ddb4c-qq27v and cart-549b8757d-7492d) were in phase Running with restartCount 0 and startTime between 2026-11-23T14:36:29Z and 14:38:04Z, i.e. started before the reported last-hour window; the cluster-wide pod listing shows the same, with only kube-system and local-path pods besides otel-demo.

The checkout Deployment configures its downstream targets as CART_ADDR=cart:8080, CURRENCY_ADDR=currency:8080, EMAIL_ADDR=http://email:8080, PAYMENT_ADDR=payment:8080, PRODUCT_CATALOG_ADDR=product-catalog:8080, SHIPPING_ADDR=shipping:8080 with KAFKA_ADDR unset, uses image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-checkout, and has a container memory limit of 20Mi.

The flagd-config ConfigMap's demo.flagd.json holds the fault-injection flags productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage and imageSlowLoad, and every one of them has defaultVariant set to "off" in that ConfigMap, so the configuration as stored does not switch on a latency or failure injection for checkout's dependencies.

For the checkout orders visible in the pod logs during the reported hour, every sequence reached 'payment went through' and 'order confirmation email sent' within tens of milliseconds of the '[PlaceOrder]' line, and the downstream pods that log their work (payment, shipping, quote, cart) handled those same requests in the millisecond range; this does not corroborate any of checkout's logged calls being slow for those sampled requests.

Rejected as an explanation for the last hour: that a pod restart, crash or rollout (OOMKilled, Evicted, reschedule) put checkout or a dependency into a degraded state. All otel-demo pods are Running with restartCount 0 and pod start times of 14:36–14:38Z, before the hour in question, and the checkout container's previous log instance does not exist (no prior terminated instance).

Unresolved candidate: the slow hop may be a call whose per-request latency no reachable source measures — the checkout Deployment depends on CURRENCY_ADDR=currency:8080, PRODUCT_CATALOG_ADDR=product-catalog:8080 and EMAIL_ADDR=http://email:8080, and the currency pod wrote no log lines at all in the window (no per-request timing), so a slow currency, product-catalog or email hop inside checkout's 12–22 ms pre-payment segment cannot be isolated from application logs; span or client-duration metrics would be required and were unavailable.

Unresolved candidate: the customer-reported slowness may be confined to a tail subset of checkout traffic that the roughly 40 complete order sequences present in the checkout pod log do not represent (the log shows only per-step timing per order, not per-request RPC percentiles), so a p95/p99 regression in one client call could exist without being visible here.

When the trace/metric backend is reachable again, rank checkout's client spans by latency for the window 16:52:14Z–17:52:14Z and compare against a pre-window baseline, e.g. rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count/bucket by rpc_service and rpc_method with service_name=checkout and traces_span_metrics_calls_total by span_name on checkout's client spans; the same ranking is what would name the slow downstream call.

Confirm whether Datadog APM is expected to be integrated for this environment, since it is absent from the data sources available to this Run; alternatively enable per-RPC client latency logging (or raise one dependency's log verbosity, e.g. currency, which logged nothing) so a slow hop can be isolated without a trace backend.

gaps: Datadog APM is not an available data source for this Run (available: jaeger, prometheus, kubernetes, elasticsearch; not_integrated lists only change_history), so no Datadog trace or APM latency data could be queried; the requested downstream-latency ranking therefore has no source of truth here.

Every Jaeger query attempted against target m0-otel-20260909 returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE: traces_list_services, traces_search(service=checkout), traces_search_by_tags(service=checkout) — so no span durations, no parent/child edges and no service-level latency for checkout or its dependencies were obtained.

Every Prometheus query attempted against target m0-otel-20260909 returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE: get_metric_names ({__name__=~"traces_.*|rpc_.*|http_server.*"}), execute_prometheus_instant_query (sum(rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total[5m])) at 17:47:14Z), metrics_range_query (sum by (service_name) rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total[5m]) over 17:40–17:52Z), get_prometheus_target, list_prometheus_rules — so rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_*, traces_span_metrics_calls_total and http_server_request_duration_seconds_count values, and any ERROR series, are unknown rather than zero, and no baseline exists for a latency trend claim.

Elasticsearch/OpenSearch returned no data: elasticsearch_list_indices(pattern *), elasticsearch_cat(indices) and elasticsearch_search(index *, size 0) each matched 0 indices, so the collector-exported log index 'otel' referenced in the otel-collector ConfigMap was not searchable and could not be used to correlate spans or errors.

A cluster-wide Kubernetes events query (all namespaces, grouped by involvedObject kind/namespace/reason) returned no_data — no events inside the authorized window — so events cannot be used as evidence for or against any cause.

Pod logs are incomplete: checkout showed the newest 200 of 294 lines (91 lines before 17:11:16Z were not read via that call; a second call covered 16:55:53–17:11:16Z), and payment/shipping/quote/cart each showed only their newest 30–40 lines, so unsampled requests are unknown.

No log lines at all were available for the frontend, frontend-proxy, currency and flagd pods in the window (containers read but 0 bytes), so edge/request-level latency, currency's own per-request duration and flagd's runtime flag-evaluation state are unknown; the flagd-config ConfigMap reflects only stored defaults, not whether a flag was toggled at runtime.

The checkout log deltas are application step timings (multiple downstream calls between log lines), not per-RPC latency; no per-call attribution of the 12–22 ms pre-payment segment to cart, product-catalog, currency or shipping is possible from the available evidence.

Alert state could not be read: the alertmanager pod produced no log lines in the window and Prometheus (which evaluates rule CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh) was unreachable, so whether any alert was firing during the hour is unknown.
next_steps: Retry Jaeger/Prometheus access for target m0-otel-20260909 (or restore it) and then compute checkout client-span latency by downstream operation (rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_bucket grouped by rpc_service/rpc_method, and traces_span_metrics_calls_total by span_name) for 2026-11-23T16:52:14Z–17:52:14Z against an earlier baseline window.

Verify whether Datadog APM should be integrated for this environment; if so, register it and pull the checkout service's downstream dependency latency from Datadog, since the question names that source.

If trace access stays unavailable, temporarily enable per-RPC client latency logging in checkout (and verbosity for currency, which logged nothing) to attribute the delay to a specific downstream call.
Ask the customers for the affected request paths and timestamps so that specific orders, rather than the whole hour, can be examined in logs and later in traces.

content:
{"alertmanager.yml":"global: {}
receivers:
- name: opspilot
  webhook_configs:
  - http_config:
      authorization:[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]        [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
        type: Bearer [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]: 0
    send_resolved: true
    url: http://opspilot-web:8080/intake/alertmanager
- name: opspilot-self
route:
  group_by:
  - alertname
  - namespace
  - service
  group_interval: 1m
  group_wait: 10s
  receiver: opspilot
  repeat_interval: 1h
  routes:
  - matchers:
    - opspilot_self="true"
    receiver: opspilot-self
templates: []
"}

{"relay":"connectors:
  spanmetrics: {}
exporters:
  debug: {}
  opensearch:
    http:
      endpoint: http://opensearch:9200
      tls:
        insecure: true
    logs_index: otel
  otlp:
    endpoint: jaeger-collector:4317
    tls:
      insecure: true
  otlphttp/prometheus:
    auth:[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]      [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] basicauth/prometheus
    endpoint: http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/otlp
    tls:
      insecure: true
extensions:
  basicauth/prometheus:
    client_auth:[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]      [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
      username: collector
  health_check:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:13133
processors:
  batch: {}
  k8sattributes:
    extract:
      metadata:
      - k8s.namespace.name
      - k8s.deployment.name
      - k8s.statefulset.name
      - k8s.daemonset.name
      - k8s.cronjob.name
      - k8s.job.name
      - k8s.node.name
      - k8s.pod.name
      - k8s.pod.uid
      - k8s.pod.start_time
    passthrough: false
    pod_association:
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.ip
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.uid
    - sources:
      - from: connection
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 5s
    limit_percentage: 80
    spike_limit_percentage: 25
  resource:
    attributes:
    - action: insert
      from_attribute: k8s.pod.uid
      key: service.instance.id
  transform:
    error_mode: ignore
    trace_statements:
    - context: span
      statements:
      - replace_pattern(name, "\\?.*", "")
      - replace_match(name, "GET /api/products/*", "GET /api/products/{productId}")
receivers:
  httpcheck/frontend-proxy:
    targets:
    - endpoint: http://frontend-proxy:8080
  jaeger:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14250
      thrift_compact:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:6831
      thrift_http:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14268
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4317
      http:
        cors:
          allowed_origins:
          - http://*
          - https://*
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4318
  prometheus:
    config:
      scrape_configs:
      - job_name: opentelemetry-collector
        scrape_interval: 10s
        static_configs:
        - targets:
          - ${env:MY_POD_IP}:8888
  redis:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: valkey-cart:6379
  zipkin:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:9411
service:
  extensions:
  - health_check
  - basicauth/prometheus
  pipelines:
    logs:
      exporters:
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
    metrics:
      exporters:
      - otlphttp/prometheus
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - httpcheck/frontend-proxy
      - redis
      - otlp
      - spanmetrics
    traces:
      exporters:
      - otlp
      - debug
      - spanmetrics
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - transform
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
      - jaeger
      - zipkin
  telemetry:
    metrics:
      level: detailed
      readers:
      - periodic:
          exporter:
            otlp:
              endpoint: otel-collector:4318
              protocol: grpc
          interval: 10000
          timeout: 5000
"}

{"alerting_rules.yml":"groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
","alerts":"{}
","allow-snippet-annotations":"false","prometheus.yml":"global:
  evaluation_interval: 1m
  scrape_interval: 1m
  scrape_timeout: 10s
storage:
  tsdb:
    out_of_order_time_window: 30m
otlp:
    keep_identifying_resource_attributes: true
    promote_resource_attributes:
    - opspilot.integration.id
    - service.instance.id
    - service.name
    - service.namespace
    - service.version
    - cloud.availability_zone
    - cloud.region
    - deployment.environment.name
    - k8s.cluster.name
    - k8s.container.name
    - k8s.cronjob.name
    - k8s.daemonset.name
    - k8s.deployment.name
    - k8s.job.name
    - k8s.namespace.name
    - k8s.node.name
    - k8s.pod.name
    - k8s.replicaset.name
    - k8s.statefulset.name
    - container.name
    - host.name
rule_files:
- /etc/config/recording_rules.yml
- /etc/config/alerting_rules.yml
- /etc/config/rules
- /etc/config/alerts
scrape_configs:
- job_name: prometheus
  static_configs:
  - targets:
    - localhost:9090
- bearer_token_file: [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]  job_name: kubernetes-apiservers
  kubernetes_sd_configs:
  - role: endpoints
  relabel_configs:
  - action: keep
    regex: default;kubernetes;https
    source_labels:
    - __meta_kubernetes_namespace
    - __meta_kubernetes_service_name
    - __meta_kubernetes_endpoint_port_name
  scheme: https
  tls_config:
    ca_file: /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/ca.crt
- bearer_token_file: [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]  job_name: kubernetes-nodes
  kubernetes_sd_configs:
  - role: node
  relabel_configs:
  - action: labelmap
    regex: __meta_kubernetes_node_label_(.+)
  - replacement: kubernetes.default.svc:443
